class.name: DeviceProfile
class.brief_description: A device preset used by the editor's resolution preview to drive viewport sizing and the active mobile/pc feature branch.
class.description: Each [DeviceProfile] describes one entry in the editor's device picker (the [code]Free / iPhone 15 Pro / ...[/code] menu in the 2D toolbar and in the Game workspace). Built-in presets live in [code]DeviceDatabase[/code]; you can also instantiate this resource yourself and save it as a [code].tres[/code] alongside the project. Beyond the obvious resolution / DPI / safe-area fields, [DeviceProfile] carries a [member device_class] enum and an optional [member feature_tags] override. Together they control which engine feature tags get injected into [ProjectSettings] (and forwarded to F5-launched child processes via [code]GODOT_EDITOR_CUSTOM_FEATURES[/code]) for the duration of the preview. The default mapping is: [codeblock] PHONE / TABLET -> ["mobile"] DESKTOP -> ["pc"] CONSOLE -> [] (left to the project) GENERIC -> [] [/codeblock] This lets scripts branch on [code]OS.has_feature("mobile")[/code] / [code]OS.has_feature("pc")[/code] at design time (in [code]@tool[/code] scripts) and at F5 runtime, without round-tripping through the export-preset dialog. The host-platform [code]pc[/code] tag is hard-coded by the OS layer on Windows / Linux / macOS and cannot be turned off. The canonical "are we previewing a mobile device?" check is therefore [code]OS.has_feature("mobile")[/code], not [code]!OS.has_feature("pc")[/code].

method.name: get_effective_feature_tags
method.description: Returns the feature tags that will actually be injected when this profile is active. Equal to [member feature_tags] when it is non-empty (stripped and lowercased); otherwise derived from [member device_class] using the default mapping documented in the class description.

members.member: Broad device classification. Used by the picker UI to group entries (Phones / Tablets / Desktop / ...) and as the fallback source for [method get_effective_feature_tags] when [member feature_tags] is empty.
Display name shown in the device picker. Should be unique within the active database; [code]DeviceDatabase.find_by_name[/code] uses it as a key.
Pixel density in dots-per-inch, used by the editor's content-scale preview to compute the on-screen size of the device frame.

Explicit list of engine feature tags this profile should inject. When non-empty, it overrides the [member device_class]-based default. Entries are stripped and lowercased before use so the project sees the canonical Godot tag form.
Native pixel resolution of the device (portrait orientation by convention; the picker UI rotates it on demand).
Pixel-space safe area (e.g. inside the notch / home-indicator margins). Origin is the top-left of [member resolution]. Leave as the zero rectangle to disable safe-area visualization.

constants.constant: Unclassified preset. Injects no feature tags by default; relies on the host platform's own tag set.
Desktop window preset. Default tag: [code]pc[/code]. Note that on Windows / Linux / macOS the host already reports [code]pc[/code] regardless of this preset.
Console device. Default tag set is empty; define your own via [member feature_tags].
